episodes.title: Singapore's Brand and Network Struggles
episodes.summary_zh: 本期播客深入探讨了新加坡航空（Singapore Airlines）在品牌塑造、机队规划以及航线网络上面临的深层挑战。三位主播指出，曾经享誉全球的新航在近期发布的全新宽体机客舱内饰设计中出现了明显失误，不同舱位由多家设计公司独立操纵导致风格割裂，且商务舱的亮黄色点赞配色让人联想到低成本航司（Scoot），严重损害了其一贯的高端品牌形象。在网络与机队层面，随着中东三大航（ME3）以及袋鼠航线（Kangaroo Route）直飞技术的普及，新航地理位置的传统枢纽优势正在被削弱，超远程窄体机（ULR）运力有限，而低成本子公司Scoot的快速扩张也在一定程度上挤压了主线网络的溢价空间。
key_takeaways_zh: 新加坡航空近期发布的全新宽体机客舱内饰因多方设计缺乏协同而遭到业内批评，高端品牌的延续性受到质疑。
新航标志性的黄色点缀和色彩混搭削弱了其传统的奢华感，甚至引发了与低成本子公司Scoot的品牌联想混乱。
随着中东三大航等竞争对手在欧澳航线上实现更强的单转机覆盖，新航原有的地理枢纽优势已大不如前。
超远程直飞航线（ULR）虽然拓展了航点，但机座容量受限，难以提供与宽体大机舱相媲美的运力规模。

highlights.title_zh: 新航是否在消耗旧日声誉
highlights.summary_zh: 主播们指出新加坡航空近年来面临诸多挣扎，开始引发业界对其是否依然配得上全球顶尖奢华航司声誉的讨论。曾经无往不利的高端定位如今正面临审视。
highlights.quote_en: What a great airline that used to be, gentlemen. But apparently, no airline can stay on top forever.

highlights.title_zh: 新客舱设计引发审美争议
highlights.summary_zh: 新航近期公布了针对A350及777-9的全新宽体机客舱内饰，但博客和行业专家对其中的商务舱设计及黄色点缀提出了严厉批评。这些设计被指缺乏统一的审美规划。
highlights.quote_en: These are interiors coming in the second half of next year on these retrofitted 350900s. And then assuming this ever happens...

highlights.title_zh: 多设计公司操刀导致割裂
highlights.summary_zh: 爆料显示新航在客舱设计中分别聘请了三家不同的设计公司独立打造头等舱、商务舱、经济与超级经济舱，彼此缺乏沟通，导致整个机舱呈现出好似三家航空公司的拼凑感。
highlights.quote_en: One did economy and premium economy, one did business class, one did first class. And it is if they designed these interiors in a vacuum.

highlights.title_zh: 商务舱黄色点缀引发误导
highlights.summary_zh: 由BMW Design Works操刀的商务舱采用了赛车风格的亮黄色点缀，这让外界联想到新航旗下的低成本航司Scoot，而非传统高端的金色或品牌基调。
highlights.quote_en: That cabin has what the airline proudly calls race car inspired styling. And what is Scoot's color? I'm going to say yellow. It is yellow.

highlights.title_zh: 欧澳袋鼠航线竞争加剧
highlights.summary_zh: 回顾历史，新航曾凭借地理位置和极具竞争力的成本优势，成功收割欧洲到澳大利亚的袋鼠航线流量；但如今中东三大航凭借强大的枢纽和广泛航点对其构成了巨大威胁。
highlights.quote_en: And you can look at the kangaroo route from Europe to Australia to really see how this played out.

highlights.title_zh: 超远程机队运力与座级局限
highlights.summary_zh: 新航依赖A350-900ULR等机型执飞超远程直飞航线，但由于客舱座位数较少（仅132座），在面对像A380或更大机型的大运量竞争时显得力不从心。
highlights.quote_en: The new configuration they just announced with this whole refresh, it's going to have 132 seats on that airplane. That's not a lot.

highlights.summary_zh: 低成本航司Scoot在东南亚和中国市场的快速扩张和航点替代，在丰富集团航线网络的同时，也逐渐挤压了主线网络提供一致性高端服务的空间。
highlights.quote_en: Scoot is growing fast, in 2026 seats are up more than 37% versus 2019.

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: I'm John Ostrower, editor in chief of the Air Current. I'm Brian Sumers and I write the Airline Observer. And I'm Brett Snyder, author of Cranky Flier.
transcript.zh: 我是《The Air Current》主编琼·奥斯特罗尔。《The Airline Observer》创始人布莱恩·萨默斯。我是《Cranky Flier》的作者布雷特·斯奈德。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: You're listening to the Air Show, the podcast where we talk about what happens in the business of the sky, brought to you by the Alaska Hawaiian Airlines pilots. This episode is also sponsored by SkyGo, along with Upgrade Inc.
transcript.zh: 您正在收听的是The Air Show，一档探讨航空商业动态的播客，由阿拉斯加航空和夏威夷航空的飞行员为您呈现。本期节目还得到了SkyGo以及Upgrade Inc.的赞助支持。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Learn more at upgrade.com/flex-pay. All right, we have a full house this week, guys. And I think it's important that we at least acknowledge the absolute show that was last weekend.
transcript.zh: 您可以登录upgrade.com/flex-pay了解更多信息。好吧，这周我们全员到齐，各位。我认为我们至少应该回顾一下上周末那场堪称闹剧的糟糕状况。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Something happen? Brett, you didn't like those press conferences? We got so much information out of them. We got nothing useful.
transcript.zh: 发生什么事了吗？布雷特，你不喜欢那些新闻发布会吗？我们从中获取了大量信息。我们什么有用的话都没得到。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: No, you're right. In all seriousness, I don't think the three of us have much to add right now. We know that something went seriously wrong last week at the FAA. It halted all departures in the US for several hours, and it was extremely disruptive.
transcript.zh: 不，你说得对。说真的，我觉得我们三个人现在没什么好补充的。我们知道上周FAA出了严重的问题，导致美国境内所有航班停飞数小时，造成了极其严重的混乱。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Yeah, uh, Friday afternoon, uh, all hell broke loose and the entire team from the Air Current was very busily uh, covering this as it unfolded into the evening.
transcript.zh: 对，周五下午，情况彻底失控，《The Air Current》的整个团队一直在忙碌地进行报道，直到夜幕降临。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: By 8:15 p.m. Eastern time, the ground stop was lifted, but the recovery and the necessity to understand what actually happened had just begun.
transcript.zh: 美东时间晚上8点15分，地面停飞指令解除，但关于恢复运行以及弄清实际发生原因的工作才刚刚开始。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Uh-huh. But as we sit here on November 18th recording, uh, we know the issue has been traced to copper to fiber replacement and a router installation in rural Arkansas.
transcript.zh: 嗯哼。不过当我们于11月18日坐在这里录音时，我们知道该问题已被追溯到阿肯色州乡村地区的铜缆换光纤以及路由器安装。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: But that doesn't answer the biggest question. Why and how did this manage to cascade across the entire air traffic control system in this country?
transcript.zh: 但这并没有回答最核心的问题：为什么以及它是如何成功导致美国整个空中交通管制系统全面瘫痪的？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: I think we're going to have to put that on the shelf for right now and we'll revisit this as we all keep digging.
transcript.zh: 我想我们得先把这个问题搁置一下，随着我们不断深入挖掘，日后会重新审视此事。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yeah, it's tempting to go with wild speculation and conspiracy theory, but I think we will uh, not do that today instead.
transcript.zh: 是的，大家很容易进行各种疯狂的猜测和阴谋论，但我认为我们今天还是别这么做了。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Hold on. Wait. Wait. Wait. Do we not have a podcast for wild conspiracy theories and speculations? Like, isn't that sort of like the mantra of 2026?
transcript.zh: 等等。等一下。等等。难道我们没有一档专门用于疯狂阴谋论和猜测的播客吗？比如，这不正是2026年的座右铭吗？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, maybe we'd have more listeners if we did that. We go mainstream and not just you airline industry people that are listening.
transcript.zh: 对，如果我们这么做，也许听众会更多。我们会走向主流，而不仅仅是你们这些航空业圈内人在听。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Anyway, moving on, this week, we are going to cross the Pacific. We're going to talk about Singapore Airlines, which apparently has been having some struggles lately.
transcript.zh: 言归正传，本周我们将跨越太平洋。我们要谈谈新加坡航空，这家航司最近似乎遇到了一些困难。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: What a great airline that used to be, gentlemen. But apparently, no airline can stay on top forever.
transcript.zh: 曾经多么伟大的航司啊，先生们。但显然，没有任何航司能永远立于不败之地。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I'm starting to wonder if SQ is trading on a very old reputation. You guys know that adage, you can fool all the people some of the time and some of the people all of the time, but you cannot fool all the people all the time.
transcript.zh: 我开始怀疑新航（SQ）是否在靠着陈旧的声誉苦苦支撑。大家知道那句谚语吗：你可以暂时欺骗所有人，也可以永远欺骗部分人，但你不可能永远欺骗所有人。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Gentlemen, I don't know that we're quite there yet, uh, but I think we're we're nearing a time, possibly unless things change, where people may realize that the Singapore Airlines they once knew and loved, the one they went out of their way to fly, the one that won all those awards, perhaps isn't what it once was.
transcript.zh: 先生们，我不知道我们是否已经走到了这一步，嗯，但我认为我们正在接近这样一个时刻——除非情况发生变化——人们可能会意识到，他们曾经熟悉并喜爱的新航，那个他们不惜绕路也要去坐、斩获无数奖项的新航，或许已经不复当年了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Startling accusations here, Mr. Summers.
transcript.zh: 萨默斯先生，你这可是惊人的指控啊。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Tell us what you're how you really feel.
transcript.zh: 快跟大家说说你真实的感受。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Yeah, no, I'm looking forward to hearing more about this from you, but let's break this into two halves.
transcript.zh: 对，不，我很期待听你多聊聊这个，不过我们先把这个话题分成两半来谈。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Brian, I know a lot of what you're talking about is related to some of the recent news from the airline. So let's start off with a branding product discussion.
transcript.zh: 布莱恩，我知道你谈论的很多内容都与这家航司最近的新闻有关。所以我们先从品牌和产品讨论开始。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: And then John and I can go into network and fleet and look at it from that perspective. Sound good?
transcript.zh: 然后我和琼可以切入航线网络与机队，从那个角度来看看。听起来怎么样？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: That sounds good, but I'm wondering if you made some sort of mistake, uh, Brett, because, uh, the nerds in this industry, including the two of you, you always think that network and fleet are the most important, and usually I get shuffled to the very end of the podcast to say like eight words about brand.
transcript.zh: 听起来不错，但我怀疑你是不是犯了什么错误，布雷特，因为，嗯，这个行业的书呆子们——包括你们俩——总是认为网络和机队最重要，而我通常被排到播客的最后，只能对品牌说个八个字。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Are you sure you want me to go first?
transcript.zh: 你确定要让我先说吗？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: I just think it's funny you don't think you're one of the nerds.
transcript.zh: 我只是觉得好笑，你竟然不觉得自己也是个书呆子。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Well, and also, I would just say there's no marketing and branding without network and fleet. So we will underpin all of this at the back end of the conversation.
transcript.zh: 好吧，另外我只想说，离开网络和机队，营销和品牌就无从谈起。所以我们会在对话的后半部分为这一切奠定基础。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: All right, I feel like we have a lot of people that are going to be fast-forwarding now to after the break. I'm going to give this my best shot.
transcript.zh: 好吧，我觉得现在有很多人要直接快进到中场休息之后了。我会尽我最大的努力。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: No, come on. Listen, this stuff matters, Brian. I am with you. It is important. It's just I live in my numbers and spreadsheets. That's my happy place.
transcript.zh: 不，拜托。听着，这些东西很重要，布莱恩。我支持你。这很重要。只是我习惯了沉浸在数字和电子表格里。那是我的快乐老家。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Uh, but that doesn't mean I'm not interested in it. And I know that this is something you actually feel pretty passionate about, uh, clearly from your opening remarks. So I'm I'm excited to to start with this.
transcript.zh: 呃，但这并不意味着我不感兴趣。而且我知道这确实是你非常热衷的事情，呃，从你的开场白中就能明显看出来。所以我很兴奋从这个话题开始。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Here's the gist. I think Singapore Airlines and airline that right now doesn't exactly know what it wants to be. And then whether you believe this or not, I really do think customers pick up on these things.
transcript.zh: 要点是这样的。我认为新加坡航空是一家目前并不确切知道自己想要成为什么样子的航司。无论你信不信，我真的认为旅客是能察觉到这些事情的。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I I disagree. When it comes to the idea of this everything premium era that we're living in, like Singapore is legitimately and rightfully in a group of elite airlines that doesn't have to remind you every 10 ft that it's a premium airline.
transcript.zh: 我持不同意见。谈到我们所处的这个“万物皆高端”的时代，新航实至名归地属于精英航司群体，它们不需要每隔十英尺就提醒你它是一家高端航司。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Not having to remind you that it's a premium airline is a huge notable difference from a certain batch of carriers in this country that constantly tell you they're a premium carrier.
transcript.zh: 不需要提醒你它是一家高端航司，这与国内某批不断标榜自己是高端航司的航司有着巨大的显着区别。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So, I'm just saying like the reputation lives and it it actually absolutely is still deserved.
transcript.zh: 所以我只想说，声誉长存，而且它确实当之无愧。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Okay, guys, uh, you've made fun of me a little bit. I do think that I've been too harsh because that's my stick and I like to go over the top, whatever. But, John, in part, I think that you have made my point because the airline that you've been flying is a little bit different than the airline that they've been outlining for us in the future.
transcript.zh: 好吧，伙计们，你们有点取笑我了。我确实觉得自己刚才有点太严厉了，因为那是我的老套路，我喜欢表现得夸张一点，随便吧。不过，琼，从某种程度上说，我认为你证明了我的观点，因为你一直在坐的那家航司，和他们在未来规划中向我们勾勒的那家航司有点不太一样。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: So, why are we talking about Singapore Airlines today? Well, guys, did you see the new widebody cabins that the airline introduced earlier this month to great fanfare?
transcript.zh: 那么，我们今天为什么要讨论新加坡航空呢？好吧，伙计们，你们看到这家航司本月早些时候大张旗鼓推出的全新宽体机客舱了吗？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Uh, these are interiors coming in the second half of next year on these retrofitted 350900s. And then assuming this ever happens, John, you can fill us in on that later, uh, Triple Seven, uh, dash nine aircraft.
transcript.zh: 呃，这些是明年下半年将在这些改装版A350-900上亮相的客舱内饰。然后假设这一切真的发生的话——琼，你稍后可以给我们补充一下——还有波音777-9客机。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: We're calling that fanfare? Okay.
transcript.zh: 我们管那叫大张旗鼓？好吧。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Yeah, I did see it, of course, and I read the blogs and the blogs, uh, were not so kind. They especially seem to hate the business class seat with that yellow accent.
transcript.zh: 对，我当然看到了，我也看了一些博客，呃，博客的评价可不太好。他们似乎尤其讨厌带有那一抹黄色点缀的商务舱座椅。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: incongruous from not only the other two cabins, but also where they were coming from on the 350, which was their most recent update. But look, I also think we need to jump to sort of the 30,000 ft level here.
transcript.zh: 不仅与其他两个客舱格格不入，而且与他们此前在A350上的客舱设计（这也是他们最近一次更新）一脉相承。但我觉得我们还是得站在三万英尺的高度来俯视这个问题。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Singapore's branding isn't about an airline, it's about a country. Like this is one of the biggest Singaporean consumer facing brands. But this is how the country sells itself to the world. This is a soft power play.
transcript.zh: 新加坡的品牌形象不单是一家航司，它代表着整个国家。这是新加坡面向消费者最大、最核心的品牌之一。这也是这个国家向世界推销自己的一种软实力运用。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Like and the airline, which is again majority owned by the state investment holding arms, is part of how Singapore attracts tourism and investment. Then it really should have spent a little bit more time designing this cabin, huh?
transcript.zh: 而且这家由国家投资控股机构控股多数股权的航司，正是新加坡吸引旅游业和投资的重要一环。这么说，他们确实应该花更多时间来设计这个客舱，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Okay, the blogs are the blogs. Hahaha, yada yada. Those guys complain about everything. They're the only people in the airline industry that can match me, complaint for complaint, nitpick for nitpick.
transcript.zh: 好吧，博客就是博客。哈哈哈哈，巴拉巴拉。那些家伙什么都抱怨。他们是航空业里唯一能在抱怨和挑刺方面与我一较高下的人。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Look, the quality of this brand for the airline is part and parcel of how the nation will be seen globally. So it's not just a an airline industry full pie. It literally is a public diplomacy issue when it comes to how they present themselves in this industry to the world in this context.
transcript.zh: 你看，该航司的品牌质量直接关系到这个国家在全球的形象。所以这不仅是航空业内部的一块蛋糕，当他们在这个背景下向全世界展示自己时，这实际上是一个公共外交问题。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: But, uh, we talked about this on the last show. I was in New York last week, I was at the Skift Aviation Forum. There were some very senior airline executives there, you know, I like the background chit chat.
transcript.zh: 不过，呃，我们在上期节目中讨论过这个。我上周在纽约，我参加了Skift航空论坛。那里有一些资深的航司高管，你知道的，我喜欢那种背景闲聊。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: This thing about Singapore Airlines messing up its cabins, this goes beyond the blogs. This goes beyond the people that like to complain about all kinds of things.
transcript.zh: 关于新加坡航空弄砸其客舱这件事，已经超出了博客的范畴。这超越了那些喜欢对各种事情指指点点的群体。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yeah, and I I spent probably too much time in New York talking about cabin interiors, but is my favorite thing in the world. And a a quick tangent here, uh guys, Air France isn't exactly a government owned airline, certainly not anymore, but it does carry the French flag abroad and that's a big deal to Ben Smith, the CEO of the group.
transcript.zh: 对，我可能在纽约花了很多时间聊客舱内饰，但这确实是我最喜欢的事情。顺便插一句，各位，法航现在已经算不上是国有航司了，当然早就不算了，但它在海外依然飘扬着法国国旗，这对该集团首席执行官本·史密斯（Ben Smith）来说是一件大事。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: This is rival executives essentially saying, what the heck did they just do?
transcript.zh: 这是竞争对手的高管们实质上在说：他们刚刚到底搞出了什么鬼东西？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: We can get into questions of fit and finish and yellow accents and a little bit. But what I heard last week was talk of one overarching mistake.
transcript.zh: 我们可以稍后探讨做工、完工度以及黄色点缀等问题。但我上周听到的是关于一个总体性重大失误的讨论。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: And this is that the airline used three different design firms to design new cabins.
transcript.zh: 这就是该航司找了三家不同的设计公司来设计新客舱。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And uh people were joking there that like the number one product executive at Air France, you know who it is, especially in first class where he oversees every single thing that goes in the cabin.
transcript.zh: 大家当时在那开玩笑说，法航排名第一的产品高管，你们知道是谁，特别是在头等舱里，他要亲自过问客舱里的每一个细节。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: One did economy and premium economy, one did business class, one did first class. And it is if they designed these interiors in a vacuum.
transcript.zh: 一家负责经济舱和超级经济舱，一家负责商务舱，还有一家负责头等舱。这就好像他们是在真空环境中设计这些内饰的一样。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Tell us. It's Ben Smith, guys. I mean you know, if you want to project a certain look of your airline, you must look at every single detail, sometimes all the way to the top.
transcript.zh: 快告诉大家。就是本·史密斯，各位。我的意思是，如果你想展现你家航司的某种特定形象，你就必须关注每一个细节，有时候甚至要亲历亲为。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Like the designers either didn't talk to each other or the airline didn't give enough direction about what it wanted.
transcript.zh: 就像是设计师们彼此没有沟通，或者航司没有就其想要的效果给出足够的指导。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: But it felt like these are cabins that belong on three different airlines.
transcript.zh: 但给人的感觉是，这些客舱仿佛属于三家不同的航司。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And I don't think that happened here at Singapore Airlines. Now, going back to business class, like okay, it's fine. It's got all the bells and whistles that people need. It's got the door, you can't live without a door.
transcript.zh: 我觉得新加坡航空这次并没有做到这一点。现在，回到商务舱，好吧，它还算不错。它具备了人们需要的所有花哨功能。它有门，现在的商务舱不能没有门。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: And I hope that if listeners have learned nothing else from me droning on here, it's that premium is as much about consistency and feel as it is about the actual product.
transcript.zh: 我希望如果听众从我这里的唠叨中没有学到别的，至少能明白这一点：高端不仅仅在于实际的产品本身，更在于一致性和质感。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Product has to be good, of course, but the important thing is it's the same all the time.
transcript.zh: 产品当然必须优秀，但最重要的是它必须始终如一。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: uh big screen, uh Bluetooth, uh it doesn't flip over anymore that had been a complaint about the old SQ seat, which I loved because it was extremely comfortable.
transcript.zh: 大屏幕，蓝牙功能，屏幕不会像以前那样翻转了——以前大家对新航老款座椅颇有微词，不过我挺喜欢的，因为那款座椅极其舒适。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: So the three firms were Priestman Goode for first class, Designworks for business class, and Factory Design for premium economy and economy class.
transcript.zh: 所以这三家设计公司分别是：负责头等舱的Priestman Goode，负责商务舱的Designworks，以及负责超级经济舱和经济舱的Factory Design。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: It's a great seat. Yeah. What are the bigger problems here? And again, people may think I'm nitpicking, but I promise you that I'm not.
transcript.zh: 这确实是个好座位。是的。那这里面更大的问题是什么呢？话说回来，大家可能会觉得我在吹毛求疵，但我向你们保证我绝没有。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: They're all reputable design firms. I think one of the things that we have questions about is whether or not they were talking to each other or what kind of coordination was happening across all of us.
transcript.zh: 它们都是声誉卓著的设计公司。我认为我们产生疑问的地方在于，它们彼此之间是否进行了沟通，或者在所有这些设计过程中究竟进行了什么样的协调。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Uh first of all, the seat is gray. It's not brown. Uh and second, that bright yellow accent on the chair.
transcript.zh: 首先，座椅是灰色的，而不是棕色的。其次，椅子上那个亮黄色的点缀。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yeah, all very solid design firms. Uh, in fact, several years ago, I spent some time at Priestman Goode, uh, in London.
transcript.zh: 是的，都是非常稳健的设计公司。呃，事实上，几年前我在伦敦的Priestman Goode待过一段时间。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Everyone keeps talking about this yellow accent and how bad it is. Okay, so sure, it'd be better if it matched the gold of the airlines livery colors, right? But is it really that bad? And same with brown versus gray, you usually love to jump on American for using Brown, but you like when Singapore does it?
transcript.zh: 大家一直在讨论这个黄色点缀有多难看。好吧，当然，如果它能和航司涂装的金黄色搭配起来会更好，对吧？但这真的有那么糟吗？还有棕色对灰色，你平时最爱吐槽美航用棕色，但为什么新航用棕色你又觉得挺好呢？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I was really impressed with the detail that the company put into designing its cabins.
transcript.zh: 该公司在客舱设计上倾注的细节让我印象深刻。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Even here for Singapore Airlines, the new first class, it looks exactly how you would think a Singapore Airlines cabin should look.
transcript.zh: 即便在这里为新加坡航空设计的新头等舱，看起来也完全符合你对新航客舱的想象。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yes, Brett, here's the thing. Singapore's main color historically is brown. The brown is the thing that we see all the time.
transcript.zh: 是的，布雷特，关键在于：新航历史上主打的颜色就是棕色。棕色是我们经常能看到的标志性颜色。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: They've got the brown leather, two-seater sofa, couples can use that as a double bed.
transcript.zh: 它们配有棕色真皮双人沙发，情侣可以把它当做双人床使用。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Uh, maybe it's not exactly my thing. It it reads a little bit too much to me like a Ritz Carlton circa 1998.
transcript.zh: 呃，也许这不太合我的胃口。在我看来，它有点太像1998年前后的丽思卡尔顿酒店了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Then the interior mostly has to be brown. Uh Americans colors uh like this country, uh red, white and blue, maybe with some silver mixed in.
transcript.zh: 因此内饰基本上必须是棕色的。相比之下，美国的色彩就像这个国家一样，是红、白、蓝，可能还会混入一些银色。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: But that has been the Singapore Airlines brand for a long time. Uh, so I'm reasonably okay with the new first class.
transcript.zh: 但这长期以来一直是新航的品牌调性。呃，所以我对新的头等舱还是勉强可以接受的。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: The problem with Americans Brown isn't the color. Brown is brown, whatever. Uh the problem is that brown is not one of American's core colors.
transcript.zh: 美航采用棕色的问题不在于颜色本身。棕色就是棕色，无所谓。问题在于，棕色根本不是美航的核心品牌色。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Okay, so good job Priestman Goode. They got the right memo, apparently. You're saying first is fine, if not dated, but still doesn't sound too bad, right?
transcript.zh: 好吧，干得好，Priestman Goode。显然他们拿到了正确的备忘录。你是说头等舱还算可以，即便谈不上新潮，但听起来也还不算太糟，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: I mean, we're going to have to have a whole episode around American uh and design choices around branding.
transcript.zh: 我的意思是，我们以后得专门出一期节目，聊聊美航以及品牌设计选择的话题。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yes, every everybody wants another what's wrong with American episode. But anyways, the other mistake, and Brett, you've talked about this a couple of times, is that accent color.
transcript.zh: 对，每个人都想听一集“美航到底哪里出了问题”。不过话说回来，另一个失误——布雷特你也提过好几次——就是那个点缀色。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yeah, uh, most of the complaints on the blogs, but more importantly at the Skift conference on the sidelines by people who have actually designed cabins in the past.
transcript.zh: 是的，呃，大部分投诉都来自博客，但更重要的是在Skift会议的场边，由那些过去真正设计过客舱的人提出的。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I I don't love yellow generally. I I think it stands out too much. It's not a core color for the airline. But Singapore Airlines owns a LCC called Scoot.
transcript.zh: 我个人一般来说不太喜欢黄色。我觉得它太显眼了。它并不是这家航司的核心颜色。但是新加坡航空旗下有一家名为酷航的低成本航司（ULCC）。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: They complained about, uh, business class. And and that's the one designed by BMW Design Works.
transcript.zh: 他们抱怨的是商务舱。那是BMW Design Works设计的产品。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: That cabin has what the airline proudly calls race car inspired styling.
transcript.zh: 那个客舱拥有航司自豪地称之为“赛车灵感”的造型设计。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And what is Scoot's color? I'm going to say yellow. It is yellow.
transcript.zh: 那酷航的代表色是什么？我猜是黄色。没错，就是黄色。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Uh, but here's the problem, guys. When I say race cars, y'all think of the Singapore Airlines brand?
transcript.zh: 呃，但问题来了，伙计们。当我提到赛车时，你们会联想到新加坡航空的品牌吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So why would you want people's brains to go to Scoot when they got on an SQ plane?
transcript.zh: 所以，当旅客登上新航（SQ）的飞机时，你为什么会希望他们的脑海中联想到酷航呢？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Not exactly. But but then again, when you hire BMW, you're going to get an automotive inspiration. I mean, it's right there in the name.
transcript.zh: 倒也未必。但话又说回来，当你聘请宝马（BMW）时，你必然会获得汽车行业的灵感。我的意思是，名字里就写着呢。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Well, look, I think this is actually a really important point here because that bright yellow stripe, and not the golden yellow that we know as part of Singapore's boutique color palette and their exterior colors of the aircraft.
transcript.zh: 好吧，你看，我觉得这其实是一个非常重要的点，因为那一抹亮黄色，并不是我们所熟知的、作为新加坡航司精品品牌色彩组合及飞机外观涂装标志的那种金黄色。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But like it does feel decidedly
transcript.zh: 但感觉确实有点……

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Yeah, it did remind a lot of people of Spirit Airlines. So, Brian, what about economy and premium economy?
transcript.zh: 是的，这确实让很多人想起了精神航空（Spirit Airlines）。那么，Brian，经济舱和超级经济舱情况如何呢？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Uh colors are wrong, boys. Uh the chair is perfectly fine as you'd expect. Uh even premium economy is probably better than fine. The problem is the colors. Premium economy gray with orange accents, not gold, not brown. Orange, uh not sure what happened there. And then economy, blue and gray.
transcript.zh: 颜色选错了，伙计们。座椅本身很完美，正如你所期待的那样。甚至超级经济舱也可能不仅是“还不错”。问题在于配色。超级经济舱是灰色配橙色点缀，既不是金色也不是棕色。而是橙色，不知道当时是怎么想的。然后经济舱则是蓝色配灰色。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: But that orange actually is a holdover from what they had on the 350 premium economy.
transcript.zh: 但那个橙色实际上是延续了他们在A350超级经济舱上使用的设计。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Great, too. Okay, I'm losing my mind. So, what I'm gathering is all the seats are better than what they replace, but you are whining about colors.
transcript.zh: 好吧，我也无语了。所以我总结下来就是，所有的新座椅都比它们替代的旧座椅要好，但你们却在这里抱怨配色。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: It's not about colors, it's about continuity. Do we have to get a marketing expert on the show? I thought that was you.
transcript.zh: 这不只是配色问题，这是关于品牌连贯性。难道我们还得请一位营销专家上节目吗？我以为你就是专家呢。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I thought that was you.
transcript.zh: 我还以为你才是呢。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Guys, it's about colors, it's about continuity. Has anybody has anybody flown American Airlines in the past 5-7 years? Because I I've told you, I'm now flying it all the time. There is nothing wrong with American Airlines product.
transcript.zh: 各位，这不仅关乎颜色，更关乎连贯性。大家最近5到7年有坐过美航的航班吗？因为我之前说过，我现在经常坐。美航的产品其实没什么毛病。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Wi-Fi is pretty good. Uh first-class seat is pretty much identical to what the competitor's fly. Uh business-class Long haul is quite good. So, why do people complain about them? It's because it's just this mishmash of non-premium colors and feel and they're not investing in a cohesive experience and I think that's the mistake that Singapore has made here.
transcript.zh: Wi-Fi相当不错。头等舱座椅与竞争对手几乎一模一样。商务舱远程航线也相当不错。那为什么人们还要抱怨它们呢？因为这只是一堆非高端色彩和质感的杂乱拼凑，他们没有投入资金去打造一种连贯的体验，我认为这就是新航这次犯下的错误。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Is that what Matt Peper told you at the Skift conference when you asked him about it? He said like the the consistency that that people were looking for? It is. Premium is not just about one thing.
transcript.zh: 这就是马特·佩珀（Matt Peper）在Skift大会上你问他时告诉你的吗？他说这就是人们一直在寻找的一致性？确实如此。高端不仅仅体现在单一的某一方面。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Well, we can also get into operational incompetence and other things, but this is not about American, gentlemen, let's get back to Singapore. So, what else you want to say here about Brant?
transcript.zh: 好吧，我们也可以聊聊运营无能和其他问题，但这无关美航，先生们，让我们把话题转回新加坡航空。所以，关于Brant（注：此处主播口误或指品牌设计），你还有什么想说的吗？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Yeah, I know I think it's actually I yes, we're way off track, but I think it's actually really important because I think in in people's minds, at least when they kind of think about what they expect from American and what they expect from Singapore, that these are at two ends of a given spectrum.
transcript.zh: 对，我知道我觉得这实际上——是的，我们扯得有点远了，但我认为这确实非常重要，因为在人们的心目中，至少当他们思考他们对美航的期望以及对新航的期望时，这两者处于整个光谱的两个极端。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: another place it can win, maybe network, or a fleet that outpaces the competition. Let's take a break now and then both of you can opine about those topics.
transcript.zh: 另一个可能取胜的地方，也许是航线网络，或者是一支在竞争中占优的机队。我们现在休息一下，然后两位可以就这些话题发表看法。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I think one of the most misleading phrases in aviation is, hey, can you just check something real quick? Oh, I know where this is going, right? Because somehow which airport has the most flights in our network, turns into three data downloads of pivot table and half your afternoon.
transcript.zh: 我认为航空业中最具误导性的短语之一就是：“嘿，能帮我快速查个东西吗？”哦，我知道这要聊到哪去了，对吧？因为不知怎么的，哪个机场在我们网络中拥有最多航班，最后就会变成透视表的三个数据下载，花掉你半个下午。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: And I think when you are so embedded at either end, it's really, really, really easy to trip and it's also really, really, really hard to change people's perception, um, if you're on the American side.
transcript.zh: 而且我认为，当你深深扎根于其中一端时，你非常、非常、非常容易马失前蹄，而且要改变人们的固有印象也变得极其困难，尤其是如果你站在美航这一边的话。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And that's even assuming you find the right data in the first place. Exactly, and you know the answer to that one question is just going to lead to more questions. How seasonal is our Florida flying compared to the rest of the system? Who was flying that route 10 years ago? How many 757 300s did A TA operate in 2004?
transcript.zh: 而且这还是假设你一开始就找到了正确的数据。没错，而且你知道那一个问题的答案只会引出更多的问题。与系统内其他地方相比，我们飞往佛罗里达的航班季节性有多强？10年前是谁在飞这条航线？2004年ATA运营了多少架波音757-300？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: But I think that that that's kind of what we're getting at here. I think we're we're outlining the challenge here of what happens when you do misstep against people's expectations.
transcript.zh: 但我想这正是我们今天想要探讨的核心。我们正在指出这样一个挑战：一旦你的表现与人们的期望不符，就会出现这样的失误。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Now, let's be clear and not every airline needs to do this whole consistency thing. The old Sun Country and Allegiant model was to take used airplanes and they would basically put them into service with the former airlines interior.
transcript.zh: 现在，我们要搞清楚，并不是每家航司都需要搞这种所谓的连贯性。老太阳国航空（Sun Country）和忠实航空（Allegiant）的模式是采用二手飞机，然后基本上直接保留原航司的客舱内饰投入运营。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: 12, the answer's 12. Well, most people don't know that off the top of their heads, John, so they have to dig, and finding the answer is enough to make you say, I'll look into that later. Which let's be honest, usually means never.
transcript.zh: 12架，答案是12架。好吧，大多数人不会对这个烂熟于心，琼，所以他们必须去挖掘，而找到答案足以让你说：“我以后会去查的。”说实话，这通常意味着永远不会。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I don't think customers cared very much because these flights were cheap and then the airline passed the savings on to the customer.
transcript.zh: 我觉得乘客们并不太在意，因为这些航班很便宜，而且航司把省下来的成本让利给了客户。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: It's so frustrating. We have more aviation data available than ever, but so much of our time goes into just finding it and putting it together instead of actually doing something interesting with it.
transcript.zh: 这太令人沮丧了。我们拥有比以往更多的航空数据，但我们的大部分时间都花在寻找和整合数据上，而不是真正利用它们做一些有趣的事情。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Those airlines though and others like them, they compete on price. That's that's the whole idea. Other airlines compete on network or loyalty. All that stuff is fine. Uh, but what does Singapore compete on? It competes on brand and product.
transcript.zh: 不过那些航司及同类公司，它们靠价格竞争。这就是全部的核心理念。其他航司则通过航线网络或常旅客忠诚度竞争。这些都没问题。呃，但新加坡航空靠什么竞争呢？它靠品牌和产品竞争。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: That's where Skygo comes in. Skygo brings decades of aviation data and powerful analytics together in one mobile app. Airline networks, airport comparisons, historical schedules, airline fleets and more, ready to explorer right from your phone.
transcript.zh: 这就是Skygo发挥作用的地方。Skygo将数十年的航空数据和强大的分析功能汇聚在一个移动应用中。航线网络、机场对比、历史时刻、航司机队等等，随时随地在你的手机上探索。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And there's a good reason for that. Yeah, SQ still has some network monopolies in some places, but when it's a one-stop journey, uh, or there is non-stop competition, Singapore Airlines is expected to have the best product in market.
transcript.zh: 这背后有充分的理由。是的，新航在某些地方仍然拥有航线网络垄断地位，但当这是一次一站式中转行程，或者面临直飞竞争时，人们理所当然地认为新加坡航空应该拥有市场上最好的产品。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So instead of spending your afternoon assembling spreadsheets, you can actually get into the analysis. Exactly. Whether you're working through a strategic question, following an industry development, or just satisfying a little aviation curiosity, Skygo makes it easier to explore the answers wherever you are.
transcript.zh: 因此，与其花整个下午组装电子表格，不如直接进入分析环节。没错。无论你是在处理战略问题、关注行业发展，还是只是满足一点航空好奇心，Skygo都能让你无论身在何处都能更轻松地探索答案。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Customers need to know what to expect and I just don't understand how this design fail happened. Uh whether the airline gave crummy instructions or whether designers uh flubbed.
transcript.zh: 乘客需要知道他们能期待什么，而我实在不理解这次的设计失误是怎么发生的。无论是航司给出的设计要求很糟糕，还是设计师们搞砸了。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And with Skygo, the answer to the next question is always just a tap away. Skygo, serious aviation data right in your pocket. Find out more at theairshowpodcast.com/skygo.
transcript.zh: 有了Skygo，下一个问题的答案永远只需轻轻一点。Skygo，严肃的航空数据尽在你的口袋。访问theairshowpodcast.com/skygo了解更多。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: But it did happen.
transcript.zh: 但它确实发生了。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Well, is this fixable in your eyes?
transcript.zh: 在你看来，这可以补救吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: How do you feel when you go to book a flight and the price has jumped $200 since last week? It makes me mad. Then I have regret, some sadness.
transcript.zh: 当你去预订航班，发现价格比上周飙升了200美元时，你有什么感觉？这让我很生气。然后我会感到遗憾，有些悲伤。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yeah, I think it's possible that it's fixable. Uh Singapore's CEO uh said he is aware of the criticism and said the airline will take another look at its cabins. Uh I am not uh well-versed in the intricacies of fixing these cabins.
transcript.zh: 是的，我认为这并非没有修复的可能。新加坡航空的首席执行官表示，他注意到了这些批评，并称航司将重新审视其客舱设计。我对修复这些客舱的繁琐细节并不十分精通。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Really, I go through all the stages of grief. Same, but Flexpay helps airlines navigate that. How so?
transcript.zh: 真的，我经历了悲伤的所有阶段。一样，但Flexpay帮助航司应对这种情况。怎么说？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: This is what I think of as the financial hedge angle. When fares spike, whether it's peak season, fuel costs, whatever, conversion rates typically drop because sticker shock kicks in.
transcript.zh: 我认为这就是金融对冲的角度。当票价飙升时——无论是旺季、燃油成本还是其他原因——转化率通常会下降，因为价格冲击开始起作用了。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Certainly, you can make some changes to fit and finish, but again, there were some people in New York that had worked on these products in the past and they told me that switching anything material at this junction, because we're talking 2027 seats, it's a lot harder and more involved than it looks.
transcript.zh: 当然，你可以对装配和表面处理做一些改动，不过话说回来，纽约有一些过去曾参与过这些产品开发的人告诉我，在这个节点更换任何实质性的东西——因为我们讨论的是2027年交付的座椅——要比看上去困难得多，涉及的面也广得多。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Makes sense, people see $600 and close the tab a lot more than when they see $199. Exactly. But if that same fare is presented as a monthly price, then the higher fare feels more manageable and people book.
transcript.zh: 有道理，人们看到600美元时关掉网页的几率，远大于看到199美元时。没错。但如果同样的票价以月供形式展示，那么较高的票价感觉就更容易承受，人们就会预订。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Well, this is actually one of the things that Julie unpacked in her feature, like trim changes are very doable, but the cost of any bigger mods can balloon into unsurprisingly bigger certification requirements and and all the hoops you have to jump through there.
transcript.zh: 这其实是朱莉（Julie）在她的深度报道中剖析的内容之一：比如内饰饰条的改动非常容易实现，但任何更大规模的改装成本可能会膨胀，不出意料地带来更严格的适航取证要求，以及你必须经历的种种繁文缛节。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So the airline doesn't have to discount to maintain conversion. They just reframe the price? Right.
transcript.zh: 所以航司为了维持转化率并不需要打折。他们只是重新构架了价格？没错。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And Flexpay by Upgrade actually has funnel conversion data showing that airlines maintain strong transaction rates even as fares increase when Flexpay is in the mix.
transcript.zh: 而且Upgrade的Flexpay实际上拥有漏斗转化数据，显示当引入Flexpay时，即使票价上涨，航司仍能保持强劲的交易转化率。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Like every tweak in fabric or finishes has to be tested and that can add like a year on top of like all the delays that they've had with the aircraft itself.
transcript.zh: 比如面料或饰面的每一次微调都必须经过测试，这可能会在飞机本身已经遭遇的种种延误之上，再凭空增加大约一年的时间。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So it's like a seat belt for revenue during turbulent fare environments. Your simile game is on point lately.
transcript.zh: 所以这就好比在动荡的票价环境中的营收安全带。你最近的比喻水平相当到位。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I was going to say financial hedge, but this is way better. Either way, it's a tool that helps airlines stay competitive without racing to the bottom on price.
transcript.zh: 我本想说金融对冲，但这个比喻好得多。不管怎样，这是一个帮助航司保持竞争力，而又不必陷入价格战泥潭的工具。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Look, a regulatory review probably on its own can last about three to four months. But all of this is happening at a time when resources for seat certification are absolutely already scarce.
transcript.zh: 你看，单单是适航审定审查可能就要持续三到四个月。但所有这一切发生的时候，座椅适航取证的资源本身就已经极其匮乏了。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: That's exactly it. This is sponsored by Upgrade Inc. Learn more at upgrade.com/flex-pay.
transcript.zh: 就是这样。本期节目由Upgrade Inc.赞助。访问upgrade.com/flex-pay了解更多。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: If they can just change the trim and the colors, does that solve it for you or is there something beyond this?
transcript.zh: 如果他们只能更换内饰饰条和颜色，这能解决你的问题吗？还是说这背后还有更深层次的问题？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: And we're back. So Brian, you've walked us through the branding issues, Singapore seems to be all over the map. So you asked the question if it can win another way. Well, let's talk about network.
transcript.zh: 我们回来了。所以Brian，你带我们了解了品牌问题，新加坡航空似乎毫无章法。所以你提出了它是否能通过另一种方式取胜的问题。好吧，我们来聊聊航线网络。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: The question to me is whether this is about colors and fit and finish and things that can be changed within a few weeks.
transcript.zh: 在我看来，问题在于这究竟只是关于颜色、装配和饰面等能够在几周内改变的事情，

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: If that's all there is, fine. But the deeper question that I have is how does something like this happen? Is there something going on at the airline? Something among senior executives that tells me that these people have lost sight of what the airline is.
transcript.zh: 如果仅此而已，那倒也罢。但我更深入的疑问是：这样的事情怎么会发生？是航司内部出了什么问题吗？高管层之间是否暴露出某种迹象，表明这些人已经失去了对这家航司核心定位的清晰认知？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: This definitely ties in with the fleet side of things and I think that stretches far beyond just Southeast Asia.
transcript.zh: 这绝对与机队方面息息相关，而且我认为这远远超出了东南亚的范畴。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Yeah, and what's funny here, Singapore was effectively the original ME3 carrier. Uh Brett, last time I checked, Singapore was not in the Middle East.
transcript.zh: 是的，这里有趣的是，新加坡航空实际上是最初的中东三大航（ME3）航司。呃，Brett，我上次看的时候，新加坡可不在中东。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And if they have, this goes much deeper than changing out seat covers. This is something that's going to be concerning in the future.
transcript.zh: 如果真是这样，那这远比更换座椅套要严重得多。这将是未来令人担忧的问题。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Uh no, thanks for clarifying that, Brian. Who knew? What I mean is you remember, was that a decade ago when the US airlines were absolutely freaking out over the Middle East carriers, uh Emirates, Qatar and Etihad, better known as the ME3 together?
transcript.zh: 呃，没有，谢谢你澄清这一点，Brian。谁知道呢？我的意思是，你还记得吗，那是十年前，美国航司对中东三大航——阿联酋航空、卡塔尔航空和阿提哈德航空（合称ME3）感到绝对抓狂的时候吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Guys, I am really happy that you gave me this much time to opine about marketing brand and product.
transcript.zh: 伙计们，我非常高兴你们给了我这么多时间来发表我对营销、品牌和产品的看法。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: You know that I love this stuff. We also know there's much more than product that makes an airline. I'm curious to Singapore have
transcript.zh: 你们知道我有多热爱这些。我们也知道，造就一家优秀航司的不仅仅是产品。我很好奇新航……

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I mean, I think you guys all heard the Spiel, right? They were going to take over the world with their structurally lower costs and the massive subsidies and this though this is the same thing they used to say about Singapore Airlines after it started in 1972.
transcript.zh: 我的意思是，我想你们都听过这番陈词滥调吧？他们要凭借结构性更低的成本和海量的补贴统治世界。但这——这就是他们过去在新加坡航空于1972年成立后对它说的那套词。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Okay, walk us through the history here, but it wasn't exactly the same, right? Quickly. Walk us through the history quickly.
transcript.zh: 好的，带我们了解一下这段历史，但情况并非完全一样，对吧？快点。快速带我们回顾一下历史。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: The yit, no. Yes. No, it's not exactly the same. But the basic idea was the same, that Singapore had a structural advantage that wasn't fair to everyone in the Western world.
transcript.zh: 当然不是。是的。不，不完全一样。但基本理念是一样的，即新加坡拥有对西方世界其他人不公平的结构性优势。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And you can look at the kangaroo route from Europe to Australia to really see how this played out. Singapore, right, small city state, not a ton of local demand, there's some, um, but what it did is it sifoned off a ton of traffic from European airlines and Qat. Uh, and this may be shocking to you guys, but they did not like that at those airlines.
transcript.zh: 你可以看看从欧洲到澳大利亚的袋鼠航线，就能真正看出局势是如何演变的。新加坡，对吧，小城邦，本地需求不多，有一些，嗯，但它做的是分流了欧洲航司和Qantas的大量客运量。呃，这可能对你们来说很震惊，但那些航司并不喜欢这样。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Traffic, yes, but this was a different time, right? These airlines couldn't undercut fares in the same way that maybe the Chinese airlines did before the pandemic.
transcript.zh: 客流量是吧，但这是一个不同的时代，对吧？这些航司无法像疫情前中国航司那样以同样的方式压低票价。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Back in the day, IATA had it pretty tight hold on fares, right? Right, but with those fares, like being at that high level, Singapore and its lower costs could then afford to go super premium because it just had plenty of room under that umbrella.
transcript.zh: 过去，IATA对票价的把控相当严格，对吧？对，但有了这些票价，处于如此高的水平，新加坡及其更低的成本就有能力走超高端路线，因为它在该伞形保护下有充足的空间。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And this is the rise of the 1998 Ritt's strategy, I guess, Brian, that you were talking about. Uh, and apparently they've just stayed there. And to be clear, they were profitable from the start, but there were still cries that this is unfair.
transcript.zh: 这就是1998年Ritt的战略的崛起，我想，Brian，你刚才说的就是这个。呃，显然他们就一直停留在那里。需要明确的是，他们从一开始就是盈利的，但仍然有呼声认为这不公平。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And Singapore was more than happy to use its geography to serve that Europe to Australia market as a weapon. Uh, and as fleets with longer range showed up, it could connect those markets even better with fewer intermediate stops.
transcript.zh: 新加坡非常乐意利用其地理位置，将欧洲至澳大利亚的市场作为武器。呃，随着航程更长的机队出现，它能够以更少的中转经停更好地连接这些市场。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Cuz if you go back, so I I went into Skygo data. If you go back to 1987, that is when Singapore had its first non-stop from Singapore to Europe, but it still served only one destination.
transcript.zh: 因为如果你回溯——所以我查了Skygo的数据。如果你回到1987年，那是新加坡航空开通从新加坡到欧洲的第一条直飞航线的时候，但它当时只服务于一个目的地。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Until then, there were still intermediate stops between Europe and Singapore. And then at the time, they were able to add four destinations in Australia and New Zealand and then connect those dots.
transcript.zh: 在那之前，欧洲和新加坡之间仍然存在中转经停。然后在当时，他们能够在澳大利亚和新西兰增加四个目的地，然后将这些点连接起来。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Singapore is just too far from North America to be a reasonable connecting point to anywhere but within South and Southeast Asia. So I went into Syrium and looked at the ARBSP data for the 12 months ending August of this year and it showed about 58% of passengers from the US flying in the local market, meaning Frankfurt, Tokyo or Singapore.
transcript.zh: 新加坡距离北美太远了，除了南亚和东南亚内部之外，很难成为前往其他地方的合理中转点。所以我查阅了截至今年8月这12个月的ARBSP数据，数据显示，从美国飞往当地市场（即法兰克福、东京或新加坡）的旅客大约占58%。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: It's not a lot of single-stop options. Today, Singapore has 14 non-stop destinations in Europe and 10 in Australia and New Zealand.
transcript.zh: 单程直达的选择并不多。今天，新加坡在欧洲拥有14个直飞目的地，在澳大利亚和新西兰拥有10个。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Well, sounds like a mega success story. I mean, like as the airline grew, the nation grew, and as the nation grew, the airline grew.
transcript.zh: 听起来这是一个巨大的成功故事。我的意思是，随着航司的发展，国家也在发展，随着国家的发展，航司也在成长。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Then a little over 20% went elsewhere in Southeast Asia, and then just under 15% into South Asia, the rest is a rounding error.
transcript.zh: 然后略超20%的旅客前往东南亚的其他地方，不到15%前往南亚，其余的则可以忽略不计。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yeah, it was. And that's the problem is that I'm using that in the past tense because, uh, back then, they were going against Quantas and BA.
transcript.zh: 是的，确实如此。这就是问题所在，我用的是过去时，因为在当时，他们是在与澳洲航空和英国航空竞争。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yeah, exactly. And there are now so many airlines that can fly you to South and Southeast Asia with just one stop. So we're back to Singapore needing people to have a reason to choose them and that should be brand and product.
transcript.zh: 是的，确实如此。现在有这么多的航司可以只通过一次中转就带你飞往南亚和东南亚。所以我们又回到了原点：新加坡需要让旅客有理由选择他们，而这应该依靠品牌和产品。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Today, it's Emirates, right? Emirates has seven airports in Australia and New Zealand, but 41 in Europe.
transcript.zh: 而今天，是阿联酋航空，对吧？阿联酋航空在澳大利亚和新西兰拥有7个机场，但在欧洲拥有41个。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Cutter has six down there, 45 in Europe. And don't forget, Quantas now flies non-stop from Europe to Perth, uh, with Sydney coming next year.
transcript.zh: 卡塔尔航空在南部有6个，在欧洲有45个。别忘了，澳洲航空现在有从欧洲直飞珀斯的航班，悉尼航线将于明年开通。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, but even then we run into this fleet issue. Singapore can't carry a lot of people on these nonstop flights. The new configuration they just announced with this whole refresh, it's going to have 132 seats on that airplane. That's not a lot.
transcript.zh: 是的，但即便如此，我们还是遇到了机队问题。新加坡航空无法在这些直飞航班上运载大量旅客。他们刚刚宣布的这套全新客舱布局改造，那架飞机上只有132个座位。这并不算多。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So Singapore is sort of this also ran in the market.
transcript.zh: 所以新加坡航空在这个市场上有点像是个陪跑者。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: This is fascinating, uh, because I talked about how the airline is losing its, uh, brand product advantage. And now you're saying the network, uh, is under some pressure too.
transcript.zh: 这太迷人了，呃，因为我之前谈到过该航司正在失去其品牌产品优势。而现在你说它的网络呃也承受着一些压力。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And this is why Qantas waited to do London from Sydney until it had the A350-1000ULR, which by the way, will carry about 100 more passengers than the one that Singapore uses.
transcript.zh: 这就是为什么澳航一直等到拥有A350-1000ULR机型后，才开通从悉尼直飞伦敦的航线。顺便说一句，这款机型比新加坡航空使用的机型能多载大约100名旅客。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yeah. And this is what happens because Singapore, obviously, the geography is not great the way it used to be.
transcript.zh: 是的。这就是发生的情况，因为显然，新加坡的地理位置已经不如以前那么好了。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Getting the 777-9 is really important for Singapore. They first ordered it in 2017 and they've been waiting effectively a decade for these aircraft to actually arrive. Uh with the A380s very much out of production and in a diminishing part of its fleet, a super twin taking over that role was really its only option.
transcript.zh: 引进777-9对新加坡航空来说非常重要。他们早在2017年就订购了这款飞机，并且实际上已经等待了整整十年，才盼望这些飞机真正交付。鉴于A380早已停产且在机队中的比重不断萎缩，由超级双发客机接替这一角色确实是其唯一的选择。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Well, the Singapore hasn't moved. The fleet capability has moved is, I think, the issue.
transcript.zh: 好吧，新加坡又没动。我认为问题在于机队能力的提升。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I do not believe they have had earthquakes that relocated Singapore. Uh, but, but Singapore is also just not that big. I mean, it has 6 million people, but that's it. It's a city state, right? So it needs connections.
transcript.zh: 我不相信他们经历过让新加坡移位的地震。呃，但是，但是新加坡本身也没那么大。我的意思是，它有600万人口，但仅此而已。它是一个城市国家，对吧？所以它需要连接。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: So SQ's 777-300ERs have 264 seats on them, and the 777-9 is going to have 300 in this new configuration. But Singapore needs an international flagship, and one that burns about 19 20% less fuel than the 777-300ER. This is at a time of painfully high fuel costs, but all the seat controversy is compounded by Boeing working to figure out when they'll actually get the 777-9 FAA certified, presumably next year.
transcript.zh: 因此，新航的777-300ER拥有264个座位，而777-9在新布局下将拥有300个座位。但新加坡需要一个国际旗舰机型，其油耗比777-300ER低约19%到20%。正值燃油成本居高不下之际，波音正努力厘清何时能真正让777-9获得FAA的型号合格证（预计在明年），这也让所有关于座位的争议更加复杂化。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: But it's too far from Europe, uh, to serve those as well as the ME3 can. And Qantass knows this. That's why Qantass has a joint venture with Emirates now to flow people through Dubai.
transcript.zh: 但它距离欧洲太远了，无法像ME3那样好地服务这些市场。而且Qantas深知这一点。这就是为什么Qantas现在与阿联酋航空开展航线联营，将旅客经由迪拜输送过去。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Singapore has a joint venture with Lufthansa, but since the Singapore market is not that big, as Qastrel on connections from Europe to Lufthansa hubs onto Singapore, then elsewhere, the double connect isn't as helpful of a joint venture when you've got a ton of one-stop options on other airlines.
transcript.zh: 新加坡航空与汉莎航空有航线联营，但由于新加坡市场不是很大，随着Qastrel依靠从欧洲到汉莎枢纽再到新加坡然后去往其他地方的航线连接，当你有大量其他航司的一站式直达选择时，这种双重中转联营的帮助就没那么大了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But even that still doesn't solve the the US problem because the publisher range of that airplane is 8,000 nautical miles. It's better than the triple 3, but it's not enough to serve the whole US market, right? I mean that they still need the A350-900ULR, and that just doesn't have a lot of seats and it's it's just not great.
transcript.zh: 但即便如此，这仍然无法解决美国的市场问题，因为该飞机的标称航程为8000海里。它比777-300ER要好，但还不足以服务整个美国市场，对吧？我的意思是，他们仍然需要A350-900ULR，而那款飞机的座位数并不多，而且它确实不是最理想的选择。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: What about over the Pacific? Yeah, it's interesting. That's sort of the opposite story because on the kangaroo route, you know, Singapore is the middle man. They they've got this hub in the middle.
transcript.zh: 太平洋方向呢？是的，这很有趣。这有点像是个截然相反的故事，因为在袋鼠航线上，你知道，新加坡是中间人。他们在中间拥有这个枢纽。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Uh, but over the Pacific, Singapore is like BA or Qanuss. Uh, it historically needed a place to stop in the middle until aircraft technology could catch up.
transcript.zh: 呃，但在太平洋上，新加坡就像是英航或澳洲航空。呃，在飞机技术能够跟上之前，它历史上需要在中间找个地方经停。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: In North America, ASMs are up more than 10%, flights are up 5%, but seats are down only 4%.
transcript.zh: 在北美市场，可用座英里（ASM）增长了10%以上，航班量增长了5%，但座位数仅下降了4%。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, and back in the day, uh, they used all these fifth freedom rights, uh, especially to North America that helped them pick up local traffic as well as what was happening in Singapore.
transcript.zh: 是的，在过去，呃，他们利用了所有这些第五航权，呃，特别是对北美地区的第五航权，这帮助他们吸引了当地客流，以及新加坡发生的情况。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: It seems like the math wouldn't be great on that one. Seriously. So this means Singapore becomes a niche carrier with the premium focus, or well, apparently lack of focus, according to you, Brian. Um, but it needs to rely on nonstop demand over the Pacific along with premium connections, but it doesn't have that many seats to fill.
transcript.zh: 听起来这里的经济账可能不太划算。真的。所以这意味着新加坡航空成为了一家专注于高端市场的垂直细分航司，或者按你的说法，Brian，显然是缺乏焦点。不过，它需要依靠跨太平洋的直飞需求以及高端中转联程，但它并没有那么多座位可供填补。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Here's the snapshot. So in early 2004, you could fly New York to Amsterdam, JFK to Frankfurt, LA to both Tokyo Narita and Taipei, and from SFO to both Seoul and Hong Kong.
transcript.zh: 这是当时的快照。所以在2004年初，你可以从纽约飞往阿姆斯特丹，JFK飞往法兰克福，洛杉矶飞往东京成田和台北，从SFO飞往首尔和香港。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And I think it's really important because I think Singapore really pushed the idea of the the ultra long haul nonstop here.
transcript.zh: 我认为这非常重要，因为我认为新加坡确实在这里大力推动了超远程直飞的概念。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Like let's let's say someone's flying from New York to Bangkok. You can fly on a nonstop to Singapore and then on to Bangkok on SQ, but those nonstops will soon only have 132 seats on them, or there's Emirates through Dubai on an A380 with more than 450 seats.
transcript.zh: 比方说，假设有人从纽约飞往曼谷。你可以直飞新加坡，然后转机去曼谷，但这些直飞航班很快将只有132个座位；或者也可以选择阿联酋航空经迪拜中转，乘坐拥有450多个座位的A380。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: When the A340-500 arrived, that was a big deal for them. And and obviously, uh, famously the aircraft that the joke in the industry was that it needed a 120% load factor to break even.
transcript.zh: 当A340-500交付时，这对他们来说是一件大事。显然，呃，业内著名的笑话是，这架飞机需要120%的客座率才能达到盈亏平衡。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: It's just shrinking quite a bit in the US. It's got these small airplanes flying nonstop. Uh, we should clarify the ULR is not on all the US routes, but it's on some of them. And then within Asia, we haven't even talked about Scoot, that fast growing low-cost carrier.
transcript.zh: 它在美国市场的规模确实在大幅缩减。它用这些小型飞机执飞直飞航线。我们需要澄清一下，ULR机型并非执飞所有美国航线，但确实执飞其中一部分。而在亚洲内部，我们甚至还没聊到酷航这家快速增长的低成本航司。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Uh, yeah. And even if it had a 120% load factor, it probably couldn't make it anyway, and it burned fuel like crazy, and also it couldn't carry a lot of passengers in the first place.
transcript.zh: 呃，是的。而且即使它有120%的客座率，它大概也飞不到，而且它烧油极其疯狂，最初也载不了多少乘客。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So four engines, four filings for bankruptcy. Now, when this first came out, right, in 2004, it didn't really hurt the fifth freedom stuff right away. It was more niche.
transcript.zh: 所以四台发动机，四次申请破产申请。现在，当这个刚出来的时候，对吧，在2004年，它并没有真正立即损害第五航权的业务。它更偏向于利基市场。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yeah, and the non stops went away in 2013 though, they came back with the the ULR. Well, they actually came back before the ULR. They came back in 2016 with SFO Singapore on the regular 900, and then the ULR showed up after, but that's when they really started trying to figure out what to do.
transcript.zh: 是的，直飞航线在2013年取消了，不过它们带着ULR机型又回来了。嗯，它们实际上在ULR之前就回来了。它们在2016年用普通的900型客机恢复了旧金山-新加坡航线，然后ULR随后出现，但那时他们才真正开始试图弄清楚该做什么。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So today it's it's mostly nonstop service to five airports in North America.
transcript.zh: 所以今天它主要是不经停直飞北美的五个机场。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: There's only two fifth freedom flights left, LAX to Narita and JFK to Frankfurt.
transcript.zh: 只剩下两班第五航权航班了，即洛杉矶到成田和JFK到法兰克福。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yep. And I'm surprised they still exist.
transcript.zh: 是的。我很惊讶它们居然还存在。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Scoot is growing fast, in 2026 seats are up more than 37% versus 2019. And it now has more than half as many seats as Singapore does on main line. And its network is pretty huge. It's all over Southeast Asia and China, but it goes out there, it does Vienna, Athens, Jeddah, into Australia.
transcript.zh: 酷航正在快速增长，到2026年，其座位数将比2019年增长37%以上。它目前拥有的座位数已经达到了新加坡航空主线座位数的一半以上。它的航线网络相当庞大，遍布东南亚和中国，不仅如此，它还飞往维也纳、雅典、吉达以及澳大利亚等地。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Um, but the real problem is that it's eating into Singapore's mainline network.
transcript.zh: 不过，真正的问题在于它正在蚕食新加坡航空的主线航线网络。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: How so? Well, I count 17 Southeast Asian markets from Singapore that used to be served by Singapore or previously SilkAir, um, but now only have low-cost Scoot. So you have fewer connecting options with the consistent product and brand anyway, like that, Brian, I'm talking about product and brand. Uh, but, but, yeah, people can connect, but they're going to be in coach on that connection.
transcript.zh: 怎么说呢？嗯，我数了一下，从新加坡出发前往17个东南亚市场的航线，过去是由新加坡航空或先前的胜安航空执飞的，而现在只剩下低成本的酷航。因此，你无论如何也较难通过一致的产品和品牌来获得中转联程选择了——就像那样，Brian，我指的是产品和品牌。不过，好吧，旅客确实可以转机，但这段转机行程他们得坐经济舱。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: It's like, Ted is back, baby.
transcript.zh: 这就好像是，Ted（美联航曾推出的低成本支线品牌）又复活了，宝贝。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: So how much of this is also related to moving low-cost labor around?
transcript.zh: 那么，这其中有多少也与调配低成本劳动力有关呢？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Scoot, I'm sure it's a fair bit just as Emirates does and the rest of the ME3. But when Scoot moves in, it eliminates any premium offering for everyone else, I mean, like a premium economy is on some planes, whatever. Um, so, you know, that's back to that that issue of you're only serving some of the market.
transcript.zh: 酷航如此，我相信阿联酋航空和中东三大航等航司也是如此。但当酷航入驻后，它就取消了面向其他所有人的高端产品选择，我的意思是，比如有些飞机上有超级经济舱之类的话题。所以，你知道，这又回到了那个问题，你只能服务部分市场。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: It sounds like it all comes back to brand again. The airline doesn't have a whole lot of network and fleet advantages. And so I think brand matters even more. And I just don't think Singapore is executing where it needs to.
transcript.zh: 听起来这一切又回到了品牌本身。这家航司并没有太多的航线网络和机队优势。因此我认为品牌变得更加重要。而且我只是觉得新加坡航空并没有在它需要发力的地方真正执行到位。
